label: Calibrated reanalysis, approximate
description: Dec 2014 replay rainfall = ERA5 reanalysis daily precipitation (Open-Meteo Archive API, sampled at each district centre) SCALED per district so its 20–25 Dec 2014 total equals the mean of the published JPS rain-station totals in that district. It is a scaling to published totals, NOT observed station data: the day-to-day shape is still ERA5's. Days outside the window are not scaled. Districts without a published station are not scaled.
method: per-district factor = mean(published station totals 20–25 Dec) / ERA5 total 20–25 Dec at the district centre; applied to every daily value from 20 to 25 Dec (value and rain6d alike)

sources.title: Prof. Ir. Mohd Nordin Adlan, 'Banjir Kelantan' (CGSS, Universiti Sains Malaysia) — slide 'DATA HUJAN' (rainfall data, JPS rain stations, 20–25 Dec 2014)
sources.note: Daily mm per station, columns 'Tarikh | Tempat Menyukat Hujan | Jumlah'. The district header row is merged across columns; each station's district is taken from the current JPS Public Infobanjir station list (scripts/data/jps/rain.latest.html), which agrees with the header. Jeti Kastam is no longer in the JPS list; its district (Kota Bharu) is the slide's header. Station elevations on the slide: Gunung Gagau 1376 m, Gua Musang 118 m, Kuala Kerai 36 m.

sources.title: ERA5 reanalysis daily precipitation_sum via the Open-Meteo Archive API (cached response scripts/data/replay-2014/openmeteo-rain.json)
sources.note: Denominator of each factor: the sum of the cached daily values 20–25 Dec at the district centre's grid point (era5WindowMm below).

sources.title: Written parliamentary reply, March 2015 (JPS explanation of the Dec 2014 Kelantan flood)
sources.figure: about 944 mm of rain over 15–24 December 2014 (Kelantan)
sources.note: Not used: the per-station USM table is more specific. Kept as the documented fallback (one Kelantan-wide factor) and as a sanity check.

districts.caveat: Mean includes Gunung Gagau (1,376 m, 1,522 mm), a mountain station far wetter than the valley; the factor is large because of it.
